Hey Robin — happy to lay this out.

My concern is that the API isn't just consumed by our own frontend. Partners and enterprise customers hit it directly to build their own audit dashboards and exports. If we emit raw UTC ISO-8601, every one of those consumers has to independently solve timezone localisation — and in practice many won't, so their users see timestamps in the wrong timezone with no warning. That's a support and trust problem.

The PRD currently specifies localised dates on both the surface and the API for exactly that reason. The engineering spec (doc.audit_eng_spec) appears to contradict this, which is the conflict we need to resolve.

I'm not opposed to *also* including an ISO-8601 UTC field for machine consumers — that's a reasonable addition. But the localised representation needs to be present in the API response, not left as a frontend-only concern.

Async is fine with me if you can document the decision either way before Thursday. If Priya wants to push back on the above, a 20-min call works too — just send an invite.
